div.l: As Austyn dyd . how schall þe worlde be ʆserued .
Lat Austeyn haue . his swynk to hym reʆserued .
Ther fore he was . a prikasoure a right .
Grehoundis he had . as swifte as foule in flight .
Of prikyng . ⁊and of hūntyng for the hare .
Was all his lust . for no coste wolde he spare .
I sigh his sleues . purfiled at the honde .
With grys . ⁊and that the fynest of a londe .
And for to sustene his hood . vndyr his chynne
He had of golde wrought . a full curious pynne .
A boue the knotte . in the grettir ende ther was .
His heed was balled . that schon as eny glas .
And eke his face . as he had ben anoynt .
He was a lorde full fat . ⁊and in good poynt .
His yen stepe . ⁊and rollid in his heed .
That stremyd . as a furneys of leed .
His botis souple . his hors in gret a state
Now certeynly . he was a fayre prelate .
He nas not pale . as a forpyned gost .
A fat swan loued he . best of eny rost .
His palfrey . was as broūn as is a berye .
A Frere ther was . a wantoūn ⁊and a merye .
A lymytour . a full solempne man .
In all the ordres foure . is ther nought oon þtat can .
So moche of daliaūnce . ⁊and fayre langage .
He had made . full many a maryage .
Of yong women . at his owne cost .
Vn to his ordre . he was a noble post .
Full well biloued . ⁊and famulier was he .
With frankeleynes . ouerall in his contre .
And with worthi . women of the toıı̄un .
For he had power . of confessioıı̄un .
As seide hym self . more than a curat .
For of his ordre . he was lycenciat .
Full swetly . herde he confessioıı̄un .
And plesaūnt . was his absolucio .
He was an esy man . to yeue penaūnce .
Ther as he wiste . to haue a good pitaūnce .
For vn to a pore ordre . for to yeue .
Is signe . that a man is well schryue .
For if he yaf . he dorst make auaūnt .
He wiste that a man . was repentaūnt .
For many a man . so harde is of his herte .
He may not wepe . all though hym sore smerte .
Ther fore in stede of wepyng . ⁊and praiers .
Men most yeue siluer . to the pore freres .
His tipet was ay farsed . full of knyues .
